intro: Chile stretches about 4,300 km from the driest desert on Earth to the glaciers of Patagonia, but averages only 177 km wide.

chapters.title: A ribbon of land
text: The Atacama Desert in the north has places where rain has almost never been recorded. Central Chile has a Mediterranean climate and vineyards. The south has lakes, volcanoes, fjords and the Torres del Paine mountains.
Ojos del Salado, on the border with Argentina, is the highest volcano in the world.

chapters.title: Earthquakes
text: The 1960 Valdivia earthquake, magnitude 9.5, was the strongest ever recorded.

keyTerms.meaning: A long sea inlet between cliffs.
